window: Monday, 5:30 am to 6:15 am. Start here even if you read nothing else
goal: The whole course built from one shop, with a memory hook on every idea. Forty minutes, from knowing nothing to knowing what every topic is for and what every term means.
drill: Nothing yet. Read it once slowly, then say the normalization sentence out loud: the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key.

goal: Question Six built from nothing: relations, keys, functional dependency, the FD diagram, and normalising to 3NF. Seventeen marks on the paper, and the method works on any normalization question.
drill: Do the StudentCourseGrade exercise at the end on a blank page before you look at the answer. If you get its three tables and two foreign keys, you can do this question.

goal: The drawing half: what the exam asks you to produce. Entities, relationships, cardinality, subtypes, then turning a drawing into tables.
drill: Every ERD scenario in er-model. Cover the answer, draw it, then check. Drawing is the largest single block of marks on this paper.

goal: The correctness half and the asking half: normalization to 3NF, then relational algebra and SQL.
drill: The 30 objective test questions, all of which live inside these lessons. Then the SQL exercises, written out by hand rather than read.

window: Monday, 11:30 am to 2:00 pm, then stop and eat
goal: The real 25/26 paper, worked question by question exactly as you should write it in the hall. This is the closest thing to the paper that exists.
drill: Attempt each question on paper BEFORE revealing the model answer. A model answer you have not tried teaches you nothing.

window: Monday, 2:00 pm to 2:45 pm, last pass
goal: One mock against the clock if there is time. If not, re-read the definitions cards and the trap list in the zero lesson instead, and stop.
drill: Re-read the definitions card at the top of each topic, and the trap list at the end of the zero lesson. Then close the laptop.
